SnapCart — Full-Stack Grocery Delivery Platform

Built a complete multi-role grocery delivery platform covering customer shopping, inventory management, order processing, payment handling, delivery operations, and real-time communication.

April 2026

Problem & Solution

Problem

Online grocery delivery requires coordinating multiple stakeholders—customers browsing and ordering, admins managing inventory and orders, and delivery partners fulfilling orders—while ensuring payment security, real-time visibility, and reliable delivery confirmation.

Solution

Built a full-stack Next.js platform with three distinct dashboards, secure payment workflows, real-time delivery tracking using Socket.IO and geolocation, radius-based delivery assignment, and AI-powered communication assistance.

System Architecture

SnapCart uses Next.js 14 for both frontend and API routes, MongoDB for data persistence, Socket.IO for real-time features, and integrates third-party services for payments, media, and AI.

Frontend Application

React.js, Next.js 14, TypeScript, Redux Toolkit

  • User interface for three roles
  • Cart state management
  • Real-time map updates
  • Chat interface

API Routes

Next.js API Routes, 27 endpoints

  • Authentication
  • CRUD operations
  • Payment processing
  • Order management
  • Delivery assignment

Database

MongoDB, Mongoose

  • User data
  • Product inventory
  • Order records
  • Delivery assignments

Real-Time Layer

Socket.IO, Geolocation APIs

  • Live location tracking
  • Chat messaging
  • Delivery status updates

External Services

Razorpay, Cloudinary, Gemini AI

  • Payment processing
  • Image storage
  • AI-powered chat suggestions

Key Engineering Features

Multi-Role Authentication

NextAuth.js with Google OAuth, credentials login, JWT sessions, and role-based access control. Each role has dedicated dashboard and permissions.

Secure Payments

Razorpay integration with server-side payment verification using HMAC signature validation. Supports both online payment and cash-on-delivery.

Real-Time Delivery Tracking

Socket.IO broadcasts delivery partner location updates. Customer sees live position on Leaflet map with route visualization and ETA.

Radius-Based Assignment

Delivery assignments consider partner availability and 10km radius from customer location using geolocation calculations.

AI-Powered Chat

Gemini AI analyzes chat context and suggests quick replies for delivery partners, improving response time and communication quality.

OTP Delivery Confirmation

System generates OTP sent to customer. Delivery partner must enter correct OTP to mark order as delivered, preventing fraud.

Engineering Decisions & Tradeoffs

Next.js for both frontend and API routes

Rationale: Unified codebase, simplified deployment, built-in API routes, TypeScript support, and excellent developer experience.

Tradeoffs: Couples frontend and backend; alternative would be separate services but adds deployment complexity.

MongoDB with Mongoose

Rationale: Flexible schema for evolving product and order data. Good fit for document-oriented data like orders with nested items.

Tradeoffs: No complex joins; relationships handled in application layer. Considered PostgreSQL but prioritized flexibility.

Socket.IO for real-time features

Rationale: Battle-tested WebSocket library with fallback mechanisms, room-based messaging, and straightforward event handling.

Tradeoffs: Requires persistent connection; considered polling but real-time updates were core requirement.

Redux Toolkit for cart state

Rationale: Cart state needs to be accessible across components; Redux Toolkit provides clean state management with minimal boilerplate.

Tradeoffs: Adds bundle size; considered Context API but Redux DevTools and middleware were valuable.

Server-side payment verification

Rationale: Security requirement: never trust client-side payment success. HMAC signature validation on server ensures payment integrity.

Tradeoffs: None—this is a security best practice, not an optimization.

OTP-based delivery confirmation

Rationale: Prevents fraudulent delivery confirmation. Customer receives OTP, partner must enter it, creating two-party verification.

Tradeoffs: Slight UX friction; considered photo proof but OTP is simpler and more reliable.

Challenges & Solutions

Coordinating real-time location updates across multiple active deliveries

Solution: Socket.IO rooms per order; only relevant participants receive updates. Geolocation updates throttled to reduce server load.

Ensuring payment security and handling edge cases

Solution: Implemented comprehensive payment verification: HMAC validation, status checks, timeout handling, and cash-on-delivery fallback.

Managing three different user flows in one codebase

Solution: Role-based routing and components. Middleware checks role; each dashboard has dedicated route structure. Shared components where appropriate.

Lessons Learned

  • Real-time features add complexity but significantly improve user experience for logistics applications
  • Payment integration requires careful security considerations and testing of failure scenarios
  • Role-based access control should be implemented early and consistently across API and UI
  • Geospatial features (radius calculations, maps) are powerful but require understanding coordinate systems and accuracy
  • AI assistance works best for specific, well-defined tasks like quick-reply suggestions rather than full automation
